name: Sill
tagline: A free app that puts any Mac window on your iPhone or iPad, with full touch control.
sentence: Streams your Mac's screen to your phone or tablet so you can tap, swipe, draw with Apple Pencil and type - useful for checking a dashboard from the couch or sketching in Procreate on an iPad while the Mac does the heavy lifting.

visual.alt: iPad showing a live Weather window from a Mac - San Francisco at 57 degrees, with a wind map and hourly forecast visible. The Sill toolbar sits at the top with Apps, Menus, Keyboard, Desktop and Settings buttons.
visual.caption: Mac's Weather app streamed live to an iPad, controllable by touch.

board.say: Your Mac app is on one screen, but you need to see or touch it from somewhere else.
You open Sill on your Mac and tap the window you want to share.
board.eg: Click the Sill menu-bar icon, pick a window or the whole desktop.

board.say: The Mac window you chose, streamed as encrypted video.
board.eg: Your Weather app, a spreadsheet, or your full desktop.

board.say: Sill captures, compresses and sends the picture in real time.
steps: Captures the window with macOS ScreenCaptureKit and encodes it as HEVC video.
Sends the encrypted stream over Wi-Fi, USB, or a direct wireless link to your device.
Receives your taps, swipes, Pencil strokes and keyboard input and sends them back to the Mac.

board.say: You see and control your Mac window on your iPhone or iPad.

outputs.what: A live picture of the Mac window
outputs.eg: Up to 120 frames per second on ProMotion displays, at quality presets from 4 to 150 megabits per second.

outputs.what: Full control by touch, Pencil, trackpad and keyboard
outputs.eg: Three-finger swipe opens Mission Control; Apple Pencil draws in any Mac app that accepts a mouse.
Copy text on the Mac, paste it on the iPad (up to 256 KB at a time).

before: You walk away from your desk and lose sight of what's on the Mac screen.
Paid tools like Luna Display ($130) or Duet ($4/month) add an account, a subscription, and a cloud relay.
Apple's built-in screen sharing is full-desktop only and doesn't support touch.
after: Pick one window and see it on your phone, with touch control, from anywhere on the same network.
No account, no subscription, no cloud server - the stream goes directly from Mac to device.
Works over USB, Wi-Fi, direct wireless, or your own VPN (like Tailscale) when you're away from home.
uses_note: Sill is 31 days old. Real use evidence is early - most coverage is feature reporting, not hands-on reviews.

coverage.title: Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad
Sill Puts Any Mac App on Your iPhone or iPad for Free

steps: [Download Sill for Mac](https://getsill.app/download) (about 3 MB) and drag it to Applications. Allow Screen Recording and Accessibility when asked.
[Install Sill on your iPhone or iPad](https://apps.apple.com/app/sill/id6816359860) from the App Store (free).
Launch [Sill](https://getsill.app/) on both devices, tap your Mac's name on the phone, scan the pairing code, then pick any window to stream.

footprint.disk: About 3 MB for the Mac app (DMG), plus the free iOS app from the App Store.
footprint.runs_on: Apple silicon Mac on macOS 14 or later; iPhone or iPad on iOS/iPadOS 17 or later. No Windows, Linux, or Android support.

best_for: Mac users who want a free second screen on their iPhone or iPad without a subscription.
Anyone who needs to check a Mac window from the couch or another room.
iPad users who want to control Mac apps with touch or Apple Pencil.
skip_if: You don't have both a Mac and an iPhone or iPad - it's Apple-only.
You need audio streaming - Sill doesn't send sound.
You need multiple windows at once - Sill streams one window or the whole desktop, not both.

alternatives.name: Luna Display
alternatives.line: Hardware dongle ($130) that turns an iPad into a full Mac display with touch. More features, but not free.

alternatives.name: Duet Display
alternatives.line: Subscription app ($4/month) for a second display on iPad, Android, or another computer.

watch: **Single developer.** Noah Saffer is the sole named maintainer. If he stops, updates stop.

**Uses a private macOS API.** The optional virtual display feature uses an undocumented Apple interface. A future macOS update could break it, and Apple won't put the Mac app in the App Store because of it.
**No audio.** Sill streams video only - no Mac sound on the device. The developer has not announced plans for audio.
**31 days old.** The first release was Sep 22, 2026. Expect rough edges.
